name: House Price Prediction
description: Residential price estimation with validated property inputs and a persisted regression pipeline.
summary: Property attributes pass through the same imputation and categorical encoding used in training. Linear Regression and Random Forest are compared before the best pipeline is saved.
architecture: A training script splits housing data into training and test sets, fits preprocessing and regression pipelines, compares R², MAE, and RMSE, and persists the selected pipeline with feature metadata. Flask loads these artifacts at startup, validates submitted property fields, and renders the predicted price and input summary.

capabilities.name: Model comparison
capabilities.description: Compare Linear Regression and Random Forest using held-out regression metrics.

capabilities.name: Property price estimation
capabilities.description: Validate numeric and categorical property inputs and predict through persisted preprocessing.

capabilities.name: Prediction presentation
capabilities.description: Show a formatted rupee estimate alongside the submitted property attributes.

stack.usage: Loads artifacts, validates form values, and coordinates model training and prediction.
Serves the property form and POST /predict, returning field errors with HTTP 400 or a result page.
Templates and CSS present property fields, validation feedback, and formatted price results.
Reads the housing CSV and builds inference DataFrames in the saved feature-column order.
Computes the square root of mean squared error for reported RMSE.
ColumnTransformer applies median and categorical imputation plus OneHotEncoder; Pipeline compares LinearRegression and RandomForestRegressor.
Saves and loads the selected model pipeline and its fitted preprocessor.

architectureConnections.description: Housing tables supply training features and ordered inference inputs.
Persisted pipelines retain fitted preprocessing for prediction.
Validated property submissions are passed to the loaded pipeline.

evidence.notes: Reviewed implementation files and repository structure during the repository audit. Only implemented behavior is recorded; availability does not imply production readiness.
